Maintenance Report — MNT-0120-004

Asset: WELL-0120 (NE-07 Well 120, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 03 Jun 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0120-0033 on 2023-06-01 Report written: 04 Jun 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0120-0033 at 07:15 on 2023-06-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.7% of the pad area, estimated 1.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 289 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 231 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0120-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.23% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0120-030

Asset: WELL-0120 (NE-07 Well 120, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 15 Aug 2026 08:00 · Finished: 17 Aug 2026 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 62 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0120-0198 on 2026-08-13 Report written: 18 Aug 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0120-0198 showed the wellhead at 33.1 °C with the air at 32.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
